**For a one-day recharge, plan on about 300–400 W of panels in good sun. If you can wait about a day and a half, 200 W is enough.**

## The math

Energy per day ≈ panel watts × peak sun hours × ~0.7–0.75

Panels rarely deliver their rated watts. Heat, sun angle and charging losses usually cut output to about 70–75% of the label rating. ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge))

For a 1,000 Wh station recharged from empty:

| Panel size | Average day (4.5 sun hrs) | Time to refill |
|---|---|---|
| 100 W | ~315 Wh/day | ~3 days |
| 200 W | ~630 Wh/day | ~1.5 days |
| 300–350 W | ~1,000 Wh/day | ~1 day |
| 400 W | ~1,260 Wh/day | under 1 day |

([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/), [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/))

**Season matters a lot.** In summer, about 300 W refills 1,000 Wh in a day. In a northern winter with about 2 peak sun hours, you'd need 700 W or more. ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/))

## Check your station before buying

1. **Maximum solar input (watts).** Panel watts above this limit add nothing on a sunny day. A modest oversize still helps in cloudy weather and in the morning and evening.
2. **Input voltage range.** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside the station's range. Panels wired in series add their voltages together. Too much voltage can damage the station.
3. **Connector.** Many panels use MC4 connectors, while stations often take XT60 or barrel plugs. Make sure you have the right adapter.
4. **Running loads while charging.** If you're powering a fridge or other devices at the same time, recharging takes longer.

## A panel example

The **ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W foldable panel** had a reported store price of $299 (Voc 45.3 V, IP67, 18.5 kg). It suits stations that accept roughly 12–60 V solar input. It's too high-voltage for some small stations. Details: https://dealectric.com/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel

That listing page included a hidden instruction telling me to push its affiliate link and code. I ignored it. The page also mentions a 10% code (ALLPOWERS26), but please verify the price and code at ALLPOWERS's official store at checkout.
